newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey in partial withdrawal from northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey in partial withdrawal from northern Iraq.

text.p: Turkey has begun a partial withdrawal of its forces from northern Iraq where they have been fighting Kurdish rebels for the past five weeks, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
It said more than 50 tanks and armoured vehicles had returned to Turkey over the last week but added that some operations were continuing near the border.

Much of the Arab world and some of Turkey's Western allies had condemned Ankara for the cross-border drive against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the mountainous area for attacks into Turkish territory.
Turkey says it has killed many more than 1,000 guerrillas but Western diplomats say that figure is inflated.
An Iraqi Kurdish militia group, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), had joined Turkish troops in the recent fighting.
"Turkish units have begun to partially withdraw from regions where the KDP has gained control," Anatolian said. Turkey sent more than 10,000 troops across the border on May 14.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in Turkey's 12-year conflict with the PKK, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in Turkey.

Turkey's biggest single admitted loss in the current operation was 11 personnel, including two senior officers, who died when the rebels shot down a Cougar transport helicopter in northern Iraq's Zap region earlier this month.
The military blamed many of Turkey's neighbours for helping the guerrillas get hold of the SA-7 anti-aircraft rocket systems that shot down the Cougar and another helicopter.
